name: Wan 2.1 ID-V2V — restyle a video from one keyframe (comparison view)
description:
Restyle a video while the people in it keep their face, expression and movement. Upload your source video and a stylized keyframe — the first frame of that same video, repainted in the look you want (make it with an image-edit workflow such as Flux Klein or Qwen Image-Edit, keeping the same framing). The whole clip is re-rendered in the keyframe's style and lighting. Add a short prompt describing what happens in the clip.

Only the first 81 frames are used (about 3.4 s, read at 24 fps), so trim your video to the moment you want and make sure it is at least that long. The result has no sound.

Width and height MUST match your video's shape, otherwise the picture gets cropped and the style transfer becomes much weaker: square 960×960, landscape 1280×704, portrait 704×1280 — or for a faster test 640×640, 832×480, 480×832. Bigger sizes look cleaner but take longer. Change the seed to re-roll.

This version outputs a comparison video: the restyled result on the right, and a narrower column on the left with your keyframe above the original clip — the quickest way to check the style took and the faces survived (about 1½ minutes at 640×640). For a clean final video, use the "restyle a video from one keyframe" workflow.
author: ID-V2V (Eyeline Labs) — Kijai reference workflow
